facts.name: Prairie Dropseed
facts.notes: A fine-textured fountain of grass with airy late-summer flowers that smell faintly of popcorn. Slow to start, long-lived.

Combines well with purple coneflower, bee balm and native grasses; in gardens with Japanese anemones.

companions.why: Purdue Extension: interplant daffodils with late-emerging, sturdy perennials such as hosta, grasses or daylilies.
Purdue Extension: plant tulips with later-emerging plants that hide the ripening foliage, especially hosta, daylily and ornamental grasses.
Combines well with blue spiderworts, blue false indigo and prairie dropseed; try it with catmint and lady's mantle.
